rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time to ensure the header reflects real-time information each time the Authorization Detail screen is displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Current System Date and Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail screen is about to be displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores them in the working date and time data fields (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent use in formatting and displaying on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Set Application Title Lines on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The screen header must display two standard application title lines sourced from the centrally maintained application title definitions, ensuring consistent branding across all screens.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Application Title Lines 1 and 2 on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress
acceptance_criteria.When: Application title lines are being set on the Authorization Detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the first application title line (CCDA-TITLE01) into the screen header Title Line 1 field (TITLE01O) and the second application title line (CCDA-TITLE02) into the screen header Title Line 2 field (TITLE02O)

rules.rule_name: Set Current Transaction ID on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The screen header must display the active CICS transaction identifier so users and support staff can identify which transaction is currently running.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Transaction ID on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction identifier is being set on the Authorization Detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the current CICS transaction ID (WS-CICS-TRANID) into the Transaction Name field (TRNNAMEO) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Set Current Program Name on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The screen header must display the name of the currently executing program (Authorization Detail program) to provide context to users and support staff.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Program Name on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress
acceptance_criteria.When: The program name is being set on the Authorization Detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the Authorization Detail program name (WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL) into the Program Name field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Format Current Date into MM/DD/YY for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The current system date must be reformatted from its raw system format into the standard MM/DD/YY display format before being shown on the screen header, ensuring date readability for business users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Current Date into MM/DD/YY format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in working date fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The date is being formatted for display on the Authorization Detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) into the MM position (WS-CURDATE-MM), the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) into the DD position (WS-CURDATE-DD), and the last two digits of the year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR positions 3-4) into the YY position (WS-CURDATE-YY), composing the date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY)

rules.rule_name: Set Formatted Date on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: After the current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format, it must be placed into the designated date field on the screen header so users can see the current date when viewing the Authorization Detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Formatted Date on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format and stored in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY
acceptance_criteria.When: The formatted date is being applied to the Authorization Detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the MM/DD/YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) into the Current Date display field (CURDATEO) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Format Current Time into HH:MM:SS for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The current system time must be reformatted from its raw system format into the standard HH:MM:SS display format before being shown on the screen header, ensuring time readability for business users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Current Time into HH:MM:SS format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored in working time fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The time is being formatted for display on the Authorization Detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) into the HH position (WS-CURTIME-HH), the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) into the MM position (WS-CURTIME-MM), and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) into the SS position (WS-CURTIME-SS), composing the time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)

rules.rule_name: Set Formatted Time on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: After the current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format, it must be placed into the designated time field on the screen header so users can see the current time when viewing the Authorization Detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Formatted Time on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format and stored in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS
acceptance_criteria.When: The formatted time is being applied to the Authorization Detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the HH:MM:SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) into the Current Time display field (CURTIMEO) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Current System Information
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the Authorization Detail screen, the system populates the screen header with application titles, the current transaction identifier, the program name, and the current system date and time to provide context to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Screen Header with Title, Transaction ID, Program Name, Date and Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to send the Authorization Detail screen (COPAU1A / COPAU01) to the user terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population routine (POPULATE-HEADER-INFO) is executed prior to sending the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header must be populated with: (1) Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) displayed in TITLE01O field, (2) Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) displayed in TITLE02O field, (3) Current CICS Transaction ID (WS-CICS-TRANID) displayed in TRNNAMEO field, (4) Current Program Name (WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL) displayed in PGMNAMEO field, (5) Current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY displayed in CURDATEO field, (6) Current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS displayed in CURTIMEO field

rules.rule_name: Display Business Message in Screen Message Area
rules.rule_description: Any business message generated during processing (such as validation errors, fraud action confirmations, navigation limit notifications, or invalid key warnings) must be placed in the screen message area before the Authorization Detail screen is sent to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Any Message to Screen Message Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed processing of a user action (Enter, PF5, PF8, or invalid key) and may have generated a business message in WS-MESSAGE
acceptance_criteria.When: The Authorization Detail screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The content of WS-MESSAGE is moved to the ERRMSGO field of the screen map (COPAU1AO), ensuring any message such as 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...', 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...', 'Already at the last Authorization...', or 'Invalid Key' is visible to the user in the designated message area of the screen

rules.rule_name: Determine Screen Refresh Mode: Full Erase or Partial Refresh
rules.rule_description: The system determines whether to send the Authorization Detail screen with a full erase (clearing the entire terminal screen before display) or a partial refresh (updating the screen without clearing it), based on the navigation context of the current action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Full Screen Refresh Required?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is ready to send the Authorization Detail screen after processing a user action
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen send routine evaluates the SEND-ERASE flag (SEND-ERASE-YES or SEND-ERASE-NO)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If SEND-ERASE-YES is active, the system performs a full screen erase before display; if SEND-ERASE-NO is active, the system performs a partial screen refresh without erasing existing content. The default state at the start of every transaction cycle is SEND-ERASE-YES, meaning full erase is the default behavior unless explicitly overridden

rules.rule_name: Send Authorization Detail Screen with Full Erase
rules.rule_description: The Authorization Detail screen is sent to the user terminal with a full screen erase as the default behavior, applied during initial screen load, Enter key processing, PF5 fraud toggle actions, and all standard navigation scenarios.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Screen to Terminal with Full Erase - Clears entire screen before display - Used for initial load and most navigation actions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The SEND-ERASE flag is set to SEND-ERASE-YES (which is the default set at the beginning of each transaction cycle in MAIN-PARA), applicable during: initial screen display, Enter key processing, PF5 fraud mark/unmark actions, and any invalid key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the SEND-AUTHVIEW-SCREEN routine and evaluates the SEND-ERASE flag as SEND-ERASE-YES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sends the Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A from mapset COPAU01) to the terminal using the ERASE option, which clears the entire terminal screen before rendering the updated screen content, and positions the cursor at the Card Number field (CARDNUML set to -1)

rules.rule_name: Send Authorization Detail Screen with Partial Refresh When at Last Authorization
rules.rule_description: When the user attempts to navigate forward (PF8) but has already reached the last authorization record for the account, the screen is refreshed without a full erase, preserving the currently displayed authorization details while showing the end-of-list notification message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Screen to Terminal with Partial Refresh - Updates screen without full erase - Used when at last authorization record during forward navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user pressed PF8 to navigate to the next authorization record, and the system determined that there are no more authorization records available (AUTHS-EOF condition is true, meaning the end of the authorization list has been reached)
acceptance_criteria.When: The PROCESS-PF8-KEY routine sets SEND-ERASE-NO (overriding the default SEND-ERASE-YES) and the SEND-AUTHVIEW-SCREEN routine evaluates the SEND-ERASE flag as SEND-ERASE-NO
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sends the Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A from mapset COPAU01) to the terminal WITHOUT the ERASE option, meaning the existing screen content is not cleared before the update, the current authorization details remain visible, and the message 'Already at the last Authorization...' is displayed in the screen message area (ERRMSGO)

rules.rule_name: Set Partial Refresh Flag When End of Authorization List is Reached
rules.rule_description: During forward navigation (PF8), when the system detects that no further authorization records exist for the account, it overrides the default full-erase screen send behavior by setting the partial refresh flag and prepares the end-of-list notification message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Screen to Terminal with Partial Refresh - Updates screen without full erase - Used when at last authorization record during forward navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF8 to navigate to the next authorization record for the current account, and the system has attempted to read the next authorization detail record from the database
acceptance_criteria.When: The read of the next authorization record results in an end-of-data condition (AUTHS-EOF is set to TRUE, indicating no further authorization records exist)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets SEND-ERASE-NO to TRUE (overriding the default SEND-ERASE-YES), and sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Already at the last Authorization...' to notify the user that forward navigation is not possible; the currently displayed authorization record remains unchanged on screen

key_functionalities.title: Screen Input Receipt
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: User Submits Input\non Authorization Detail Screen])
    B{Is this a\nRe-entry to Screen?}
    C[Accept User Input\nfrom Authorization\nDetail Screen]
    D[Capture All Screen Fields\nIncluding Any User\nKeystrokes or Selections]
    E([Proceed to\nKeystroke Evaluation])
    F([First Entry:\nSkip Input Receipt\nLoad Fresh Screen Data])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Screen Already Displayed| C
    B -->|No - First Time Display| F
    C --> D
    D --> E

rules.rule_name: Determine Screen Re-Entry Status for Authorization Detail Screen
rules.rule_description: The system evaluates whether the Authorization Detail screen has been previously displayed to the user in the current session. This determination controls whether the system should accept new user input or load and display fresh authorization data for the first time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this a Re-entry to Screen?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user session is active with a valid communication area (session data is present), and the Authorization Detail screen processing is initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks the program re-entry indicator (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) in the session communication area to determine if the Authorization Detail screen has already been displayed to the user in this session
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the re-entry indicator shows this is NOT a re-entry (first time display), the system marks the session as re-entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE) and routes to the first-time display path; If the re-entry indicator shows this IS a re-entry (screen was already displayed), the system routes to the screen input receipt path to accept user input

rules.rule_name: Bypass Input Receipt on First-Time Authorization Detail Screen Display
rules.rule_description: When the Authorization Detail screen is being displayed for the first time in a session, the system bypasses the user input receipt step and instead directly loads and displays the authorization data. No user input is expected or collected on the initial screen display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: First Entry: Skip Input Receipt Load Fresh Screen Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user session is active with valid session data, and the program re-entry indicator (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to FALSE indicating the Authorization Detail screen has not yet been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects this is the first time the Authorization Detail screen is being presented to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips the screen input receipt step entirely, marks the session as re-entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE to flag future visits as re-entries), proceeds directly to load the authorization record data using the account ID and selected authorization key from the session, and sends the populated Authorization Detail screen to the user

rules.rule_name: Accept User Input from Authorization Detail Screen on Re-Entry
rules.rule_description: When the user has already been presented with the Authorization Detail screen and submits input (by pressing a key), the system must collect all data entered or selected by the user from the screen before processing any actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Accept User Input from Authorization Detail Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A within mapset COPAU01) has been previously displayed to the user, and the program re-entry indicator (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is TRUE indicating a re-entry
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits input by pressing any key on the Authorization Detail screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system accepts and captures all user input from the Authorization Detail screen into the screen input data area (COPAU1AI), making all submitted field values and keystrokes available for subsequent processing and keystroke evaluation

rules.rule_name: Capture All Screen Fields Including User Keystrokes and Selections
rules.rule_description: The system captures the complete set of screen fields submitted by the user, including all data fields and the specific attention key (function key or Enter) pressed. This captured data forms the basis for all subsequent business processing decisions such as fraud marking, navigation, or data refresh.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture All Screen Fields Including Any User Keystrokes or Selections

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted input on the Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A, mapset COPAU01) and the system has initiated the input receipt process
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the screen data from the Authorization Detail screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: All screen field values entered or displayed on the Authorization Detail screen are captured into the input map data area (COPAU1AI), and the specific attention identifier (the key pressed by the user, such as ENTER, PF3, PF5, PF8, or any other key) is recorded and made available for keystroke evaluation to determine the next business action to perform

key_functionalities.title: Date and Time Formatting
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

    C[Extract Year digits\nfrom positions 1 and 2]
    D[Extract Month digits\nfrom positions 3 and 4]
    E[Extract Day digits\nfrom positions 5 and 6]
    F[Reassemble Date\ninto MM/DD/YY display format]
    G[Move Formatted Date\nto Screen Date Field]
    H[Read Authorization Original Time\nin HHMMSS format\nfrom Authorization Record]
    I[Place Hours digits\ninto Time display\npositions 1-2]
    J[Place Minutes digits\ninto Time display\npositions 4-5\nColon separator at position 3]
    K[Place Seconds digits\ninto Time display\npositions 7-8\nColon separator at position 6]
    L[Move Formatted Time\nHH:MM:SS\nto Screen Time Field]
    M([End: Date and Time\nReady for Display])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K --> L

rules.rule_name: Extract Year Component from Authorization Original Date
rules.rule_description: The authorization original date is stored in YYMMDD format. The year component occupies the first two characters and must be extracted separately before the date can be reformatted for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Year digits from positions 1 and 2

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original date stored in YYMMDD format in the Authorization Original Date field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization date for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first two characters (positions 1-2) of the Authorization Original Date field, representing the Year (YY), are extracted and placed into the Year component of the display date working field (WS-CURDATE-YY)

rules.rule_name: Extract Month Component from Authorization Original Date
rules.rule_description: The authorization original date is stored in YYMMDD format. The month component occupies characters 3 and 4 and must be extracted separately before the date can be reformatted for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Month digits from positions 3 and 4

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original date stored in YYMMDD format in the Authorization Original Date field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization date for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: Characters at positions 3-4 of the Authorization Original Date field, representing the Month (MM), are extracted and placed into the Month component of the display date working field (WS-CURDATE-MM)

rules.rule_name: Extract Day Component from Authorization Original Date
rules.rule_description: The authorization original date is stored in YYMMDD format. The day component occupies characters 5 and 6 and must be extracted separately before the date can be reformatted for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Day digits from positions 5 and 6

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original date stored in YYMMDD format in the Authorization Original Date field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization date for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: Characters at positions 5-6 of the Authorization Original Date field, representing the Day (DD), are extracted and placed into the Day component of the display date working field (WS-CURDATE-DD)

rules.rule_name: Reassemble Authorization Date into MM/DD/YY Display Format
rules.rule_description: After extracting the individual year, month, and day components from the YYMMDD stored format, the system reassembles them into the MM/DD/YY display format required for the authorization detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reassemble Date into MM/DD/YY display format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Year (WS-CURDATE-YY), Month (WS-CURDATE-MM), and Day (WS-CURDATE-DD) components have been individually extracted from the Authorization Original Date
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assembles the date for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The three extracted components are combined into the MM/DD/YY display format and stored in the authorization date display working field (WS-AUTH-DATE), where Month appears first, followed by Day, followed by Year, with slash separators

rules.rule_name: Move Formatted Authorization Date to Screen Display Field
rules.rule_description: Once the authorization date has been reformatted into MM/DD/YY format, it must be transferred to the screen output field so it is visible to the user on the Authorization Detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move Formatted Date to Screen Date Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization date has been successfully reformatted into MM/DD/YY format and stored in the authorization date display working field (WS-AUTH-DATE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the Authorization Detail screen fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted MM/DD/YY authorization date is moved to the screen Authorization Date output field (AUTHDTO) for display to the user

rules.rule_name: Extract and Place Hours Component into Time Display Field
rules.rule_description: The authorization original time is stored in HHMMSS format. The hours component (positions 1-2) must be extracted and placed into the first two positions of the formatted time display field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Hours digits into Time display positions 1-2

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original time stored in HHMMSS format in the Authorization Original Time field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization time for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first two characters (positions 1-2) of the Authorization Original Time field, representing Hours (HH), are placed into positions 1-2 of the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME), which will form the HH portion of the HH:MM:SS display format

rules.rule_name: Extract and Place Minutes Component into Time Display Field with Colon Separator
rules.rule_description: The authorization original time is stored in HHMMSS format. The minutes component (positions 3-4 of source) must be placed into positions 4-5 of the display field, with a colon separator implicitly occupying position 3 of the display field between hours and minutes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Minutes digits into Time display positions 4-5, Colon separator at position 3

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original time stored in HHMMSS format, and the Hours component has already been placed into positions 1-2 of the time display working field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization time for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: Characters at positions 3-4 of the Authorization Original Time field, representing Minutes (MM), are placed into positions 4-5 of the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME), leaving position 3 as a colon separator between Hours and Minutes in the resulting HH:MM:SS format

rules.rule_name: Extract and Place Seconds Component into Time Display Field with Colon Separator
rules.rule_description: The authorization original time is stored in HHMMSS format. The seconds component (positions 5-6 of source) must be placed into positions 7-8 of the display field, with a colon separator implicitly occupying position 6 of the display field between minutes and seconds.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Seconds digits into Time display positions 7-8, Colon separator at position 6

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original time stored in HHMMSS format, and the Hours and Minutes components have already been placed into the time display working field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization time for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: Characters at positions 5-6 of the Authorization Original Time field, representing Seconds (SS), are placed into positions 7-8 of the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME), leaving position 6 as a colon separator between Minutes and Seconds, completing the HH:MM:SS display format

rules.rule_name: Move Formatted Authorization Time to Screen Display Field
rules.rule_description: Once the authorization time has been fully assembled into HH:MM:SS format with colon separators, it must be transferred to the screen output field so it is visible to the user on the Authorization Detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move Formatted Time HH:MM:SS to Screen Time Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization time has been successfully assembled into HH:MM:SS format with colon separators at positions 3 and 6, stored in the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the Authorization Detail screen fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The fully formatted HH:MM:SS authorization time is moved to the screen Authorization Time output field (AUTHTMO) for display to the user

key_functionalities.title: Card Expiry Date Formatting
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Format Card Expiry Date])
    B[Read Card Expiry Date\nfrom Authorization Record\nin MMYY format]
    C[Extract Month Portion\nFirst 2 characters of\nCard Expiry Date]
    D[Insert Slash Separator\nas 3rd character\nfor display]
    E[Extract Year Portion\nLast 2 characters of\nCard Expiry Date]
    F[Combine to form\nFormatted Expiry Date\nin MM/YY display format]
    G([End: Display Formatted\nCard Expiry Date on Screen])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Format Card Expiry Date for Display in MM/YY Format
rules.rule_description: When displaying authorization details on screen, the card expiry date stored in the system in MMYY format must be reformatted into a human-readable MM/YY display format by extracting the month and year portions separately and inserting a slash separator between them.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Expiry Date Formatting - Format card expiry date by inserting a slash separator between month and year for display

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization record has been successfully retrieved and contains a Card Expiry Date stored in 4-character MMYY format (where the first 2 characters represent the month and the last 2 characters represent the year), and the error flag is not set (authorization details are eligible for display)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the authorization detail screen with the card expiry date field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Extract the first 2 characters of the stored Card Expiry Date as the Month portion and place them in display positions 1-2 of the Card Expiry Date display field (CRDEXPO); (2) Insert a forward slash '/' character as the 3rd character of the Card Expiry Date display field (CRDEXPO) as a separator; (3) Extract the last 2 characters of the stored Card Expiry Date as the Year portion and place them in display positions 4-5 of the Card Expiry Date display field (CRDEXPO); resulting in the Card Expiry Date being displayed on screen in MM/YY format (e.g., a stored value of '1226' is displayed as '12/26')

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail View program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts processing any user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to OFF, the screen erase flag is set to YES, the general message field is cleared to spaces, and the error message output field on the screen (ERRMSGO) is cleared to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution, error indicators, screen erase flags, and message fields are reset to their default states to ensure a clean processing environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail View program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No communication area exists from a prior session (EIBCALEN = 0)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The communication area is initialized to empty values, the destination program is set to the Authorization Summary program (WS-PGM-AUTH-SMRY), and control is transferred to the Authorization Summary screen via XCTL, passing the initialized communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: New Session Redirect to Authorization Summary
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Authorization Detail program is invoked for the first time with no prior session data, the system redirects the user to the Authorization Summary screen without displaying any detail.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid session exists (EIBCALEN > 0) and the program has not yet been re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user arrives at the Authorization Detail screen for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program marks the session as re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER = TRUE), performs the Enter key processing to read and populate authorization details, and sends the Authorization Detail screen to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Entry Authorization Detail Load
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the first entry to the Authorization Detail screen (arriving from the Authorization Summary), the system automatically loads and displays the authorization details for the pre-selected authorization record without waiting for user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Authorization Detail screen and the session is in re-entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Authorization Summary program (WS-PGM-AUTH-SMRY), the current transaction ID is recorded as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), the current program is recorded as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM = WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL), the program context is set to zero, the entry flag is set to ENTER mode, and control is transferred to the Authorization Summary program via XCTL with the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Authorization Summary via PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Authorization Detail screen, the system navigates back to the Authorization Summary screen, preserving the session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Authorization Detail screen and the session is in re-entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF5 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs the fraud mark/unmark process (MARK-AUTH-FRAUD) and then refreshes the Authorization Detail screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark or Unmark Authorization as Fraud via PF5
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF5, the system toggles the fraud status of the currently displayed authorization record — confirming fraud if not already flagged, or removing the fraud flag if already confirmed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Authorization Detail screen and the session is in re-entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF8 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs the PF8 navigation process (PROCESS-PF8-KEY) and then refreshes the Authorization Detail screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Next Authorization via PF8
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8, the system advances to the next sequential authorization record for the same account and displays its details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen and the session is in re-entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER, PF3, PF5, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs Enter key processing to reload the current authorization data, sets the message field to the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and sends the Authorization Detail screen back to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Message Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than ENTER, PF3, PF5, or PF8, the system displays an invalid key message and refreshes the screen without changing any data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Enter key processing is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the account ID and selected authorization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is numeric AND the selected authorization key (CDEMO-CPVD-PAU-SELECTED) is not spaces and not low-values, the system proceeds to read the authorization record from the database; otherwise, the error flag is set to ON and no database read is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Record Retrieval Prerequisite Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading an authorization record, the system validates that a valid account ID and a selected authorization key are present. If either is missing or invalid, an error is flagged and no database read is attempted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account ID and authorization key are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the authorization records from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: First, the Authorization Summary record (PAUTSUM0) is retrieved using the Account ID (PA-ACCT-ID); if found, the Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) is retrieved using the Authorization Key (PA-AUTHORIZATION-KEY / PAUT9CTS); if the summary or detail record is not found or the end of the database is reached, the end-of-records flag (AUTHS-EOF) is set to TRUE; if successfully read, the not-end-of-records flag (AUTHS-NOT-EOF) is set to TRUE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Summary and Detail Record Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads the authorization summary record from the PAUTSUM0 IMS segment and then reads the specific authorization detail record from the PAUTDTL1 IMS segment using the account ID and authorization key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current authorization record has been successfully read from PAUTDTL1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next sequential authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) is retrieved sequentially; if a next record exists, the not-end-of-records flag (AUTHS-NOT-EOF) is set to TRUE; if no more records exist (segment not found or end of database), the end-of-records flag (AUTHS-EOF) is set to TRUE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Next Authorization Detail Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: After reading the current authorization record, the system attempts to read the next sequential authorization detail record (PAUTDTL1) for the same account to support forward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user pressed PF8 to navigate to the next authorization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-records flag (AUTHS-EOF) is TRUE after attempting to read the next record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen erase flag is set to NO (current screen content is preserved without erasing), and the message 'Already at the last Authorization...' is displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: End of Authorization Records Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to navigate forward past the last authorization record, the system informs the user they are already at the last record and retains the current screen content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error flag is OFF (ERR-FLG-OFF is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following fields are populated on the screen: card number (PA-CARD-NUM to CARDNUMO), authorization date (formatted), authorization time (formatted), approved amount (PA-APPROVED-AMT to AUTHAMTO), response code interpretation, decline reason, processing code (PA-PROCESSING-CODE to AUTHCDO), POS entry mode (PA-POS-ENTRY-MODE to POSEMDO), message source (PA-MESSAGE-SOURCE to AUTHSRCO), merchant category code (PA-MERCHANT-CATAGORY-CODE to MCCCDO), card expiry date (formatted), authorization type (PA-AUTH-TYPE to AUTHTYPO), transaction ID (PA-TRANSACTION-ID to TRNIDO), match status (PA-MATCH-STATUS to AUTHMTCO), fraud status, merchant name (PA-MERCHANT-NAME to MERNAMEO), merchant ID (PA-MERCHANT-ID to MERIDO), merchant city (PA-MERCHANT-CITY to MERCITYO), merchant state (PA-MERCHANT-STATE to MERSTO), and merchant zip (PA-MERCHANT-ZIP to MERZIPO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Display Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no error condition exists, all authorization detail fields are populated on the screen from the retrieved authorization record data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been retrieved and the error flag is OFF
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the authorization response code (PA-AUTH-RESP-CODE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the response code is '00', the status field (AUTHRSPO) is set to 'A' (Approved) and the field color (AUTHRSPC) is set to GREEN; if the response code is anything other than '00', the status field (AUTHRSPO) is set to 'D' (Declined) and the field color (AUTHRSPC) is set to RED

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Response Code Interpretation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system interprets the authorization response code and displays the approval status with color coding — green for approved and red for declined.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been retrieved and the error flag is OFF
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the decline reason table (WS-DECLINE-REASON-TAB) for a matching entry where DECL-CODE equals PA-AUTH-RESP-REASON
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a matching entry is found, the reason code (PA-AUTH-RESP-REASON) is placed in positions 1-4 of AUTHRSNO, a '-' separator is placed in position 5, and the matching description (DECL-DESC) is placed starting at position 6; if no matching entry is found, '9999' is placed in positions 1-4 of AUTHRSNO, a '-' separator is placed in position 5, and 'ERROR' is placed starting at position 6

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system looks up the authorization decline reason code in a predefined decline reason table and displays the corresponding description. If the reason code is not found, a default error indicator is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been retrieved and the error flag is OFF
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the fraud status of the authorization record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the authorization is marked as fraud confirmed (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED) OR has had fraud removed (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED), the fraud indicator field (AUTHFRDO) is populated with: the fraud flag (PA-AUTH-FRAUD) in position 1, a '-' separator in position 2, and the fraud report date (PA-FRAUD-RPT-DATE) starting at position 3; if neither condition is true, the fraud indicator field (AUTHFRDO) is set to '-' only

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fraud Status Display on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system displays the fraud status of the authorization, showing the fraud flag and report date if fraud has been confirmed or removed, or a dash if no fraud action has been taken.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF5 to toggle the fraud status of the current authorization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the current authorization record and evaluates its fraud status (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the authorization is currently marked as fraud confirmed (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED is TRUE), the fraud flag is set to removed (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED = TRUE) and the action indicator is set to remove fraud (WS-REMOVE-FRAUD = TRUE); if the authorization is NOT currently marked as fraud confirmed, the fraud flag is set to confirmed (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED = TRUE) and the action indicator is set to report fraud (WS-REPORT-FRAUD = TRUE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fraud Confirmation Toggle Logic
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user requests a fraud status change (PF5), the system reads the current authorization record and toggles the fraud status — removing the fraud flag if already confirmed, or confirming fraud if not yet flagged.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The fraud status has been toggled (confirmed or removed) for the current authorization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calls the external fraud processing program (WS-PGM-AUTH-FRAUD) via CICS LINK
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization detail record (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS) is copied to the fraud data workspace (WS-FRAUD-AUTH-RECORD), the account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is set in the fraud data area (WS-FRD-ACCT-ID), the customer ID (CDEMO-CUST-ID) is set in the fraud data area (WS-FRD-CUST-ID), and the fraud program is called with the complete fraud data communication area (WS-FRAUD-DATA)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fraud Processing Delegation to External Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: After toggling the fraud status, the system delegates the fraud processing to an external fraud management program, passing the full authorization details, account ID, and customer ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external fraud processing program has been called
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS LINK call returns a NORMAL response AND the fraud program reports a successful update (WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs the authorization detail record update (UPDATE-AUTH-DETAILS) to save the fraud status change to the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fraud Update Success Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external fraud program confirms a successful update, the system proceeds to save the updated authorization record to the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external fraud processing program has been called
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either the CICS LINK call returns a non-NORMAL response, OR the CICS LINK call succeeds but the fraud program reports an unsuccessful update (WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the fraud program returned an unsuccessful update, the fraud program's action message (WS-FRD-ACT-MSG) is moved to the display message field (WS-MESSAGE) and a rollback is performed; if the CICS LINK call itself failed, a rollback is performed without a specific fraud program message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fraud Update Failure Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external fraud program reports a failure or the CICS call itself fails, the system rolls back all changes and displays an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external fraud program has confirmed a successful fraud status update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system replaces the authorization detail record in the database (REPL on PAUTDTL1 segment)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the database update is successful, a transaction commit (syncpoint) is performed, and if the fraud was removed the message 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...' is displayed; if the fraud was confirmed the message 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...' is displayed; if the database update fails, a rollback is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Record Update in Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful fraud status toggle confirmed by the external fraud program, the updated authorization detail record is saved back to the PAUTDTL1 IMS segment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization detail record has been successfully updated in the PAUTDTL1 database segment
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database replace operation completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A CICS SYNCPOINT is issued to permanently commit all database changes made during the current transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Commit After Successful Fraud Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful authorization detail record update in the database, all changes are permanently committed to ensure data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fraud status toggle operation is in progress
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any of the following failure conditions occur: the CICS LINK call to the fraud program returns a non-NORMAL response, the fraud program reports an unsuccessful update, or the database replace operation fails
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A CICS SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK is issued to undo all database changes made during the current transaction, ensuring no partial updates are committed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Rollback on Fraud Processing Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any step in the fraud update process fails — either the external fraud program call, the fraud program's own processing, or the database update — all changes are rolled back to maintain data consistency.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All authorization detail fields and header information have been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Authorization Detail screen (MAP COPAU1A, MAPSET COPAU01)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current message (WS-MESSAGE) is moved to the screen error message field (ERRMSGO), the cursor is positioned at the card number field (CARDNUML = -1); if the screen erase flag is YES (SEND-ERASE-YES), the screen is sent with ERASE to clear the previous terminal content; if the screen erase flag is NO (SEND-ERASE-NO), the screen is sent without erasing the previous terminal content

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: After populating all screen fields, the system sends the Authorization Detail screen to the user's terminal, with or without erasing the previous screen content based on the erase flag.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The session is in re-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes any user keystroke on the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives the screen input data from MAP COPAU1A (MAPSET COPAU01) into the input area (COPAU1AI) before evaluating which key was pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Input Receipt
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user is in a re-entry session, the system receives the user's input from the Authorization Detail screen before processing any keystrokes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been retrieved and the error flag is OFF
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the authorization date and time for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization date (PA-AUTH-ORIG-DATE) stored as YYMMDD is reformatted: positions 1-2 (YY) go to WS-CURDATE-YY, positions 3-4 (MM) go to WS-CURDATE-MM, positions 5-6 (DD) go to WS-CURDATE-DD, and the result is assembled as MM/DD/YY in WS-AUTH-DATE and moved to AUTHDTO; the authorization time (PA-AUTH-ORIG-TIME) is formatted: positions 1-2 (HH) go to WS-AUTH-TIME positions 1-2, positions 3-4 (MM) go to WS-AUTH-TIME positions 4-5, positions 5-6 (SS) go to WS-AUTH-TIME positions 7-8, and the result is moved to AUTHTMO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Date Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization origination date stored in YYMMDD format is reformatted to MM/DD/YY for display, and the authorization time is formatted with colon separators as HH:MM:SS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been retrieved and the error flag is OFF
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the card expiry date for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first 2 characters of PA-CARD-EXPIRY-DATE (month) are moved to positions 1-2 of CRDEXPO, a '/' separator is placed in position 3 of CRDEXPO, and the last 2 characters of PA-CARD-EXPIRY-DATE (year) are moved to positions 4-5 of CRDEXPO, resulting in a MM/YY display format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Expiry Date Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card expiry date stored without a separator is formatted with a slash between the month and year for display purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail screen is about to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date and time are retrieved, the application title lines (CCDA-TITLE01, CCDA-TITLE02) are moved to the screen title fields (TITLE01O, TITLE02O), the current CICS transaction ID (WS-CICS-TRANID) is moved to the transaction name field (TRNNAMEO), the program name (WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL) is moved to the program name field (PGMNAMEO), the current date is formatted as MM/DD/YY and moved to the current date field (CURDATEO), and the current time is formatted as HH:MM:SS and moved to the current time field (CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Population with Current Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Authorization Detail screen is displayed, the header is refreshed with the current system date and time, application titles, transaction name, and program name.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail View program has just been invoked and is beginning a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its working state before performing any business processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Error Flag (ERR-FLG) must be set to OFF, indicating no error condition exists at the start of processing, so that subsequent business logic evaluates data freshly without any carry-over error state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Error Flag to No-Error State at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of every program execution cycle, the error flag must be reset to its OFF (no-error) state to ensure no residual error condition from a prior interaction affects the current processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail View program has just been invoked and is beginning a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its display control settings before sending any screen output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Screen Erase Flag (SEND-ERASE-YES) must be set to YES, enabling a full screen erase and redraw when the Authorization Detail screen is subsequently sent to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable Full Screen Refresh at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of every program execution cycle, the screen erase flag must be set to YES so that the Authorization Detail screen is fully refreshed (erased and redrawn) when displayed, ensuring no stale data from a prior screen remains visible to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail View program has just been invoked and is beginning a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its internal message storage before performing any business processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE) must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring it contains no residual message content from any prior program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Internal Message Field at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of every program execution cycle, the internal working storage message field must be cleared to spaces to ensure no residual message text from a prior interaction is inadvertently carried forward and displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail View program has just been invoked and is beginning a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its screen output fields before sending any display to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen error message display field (ERRMSGO on screen map COPAU1AO) must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring no prior error message text is carried over and displayed on the Authorization Detail screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Error Message Display Field at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of every program execution cycle, the error message display field on the Authorization Detail screen must be cleared to spaces, ensuring no prior error message is visible to the user when the screen is refreshed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No prior session communication area exists (session data length is zero, indicating no prior interaction data was passed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a new session and initiates the new session redirect workflow, bypassing normal screen processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect New Session on Authorization Detail Screen Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user is accessing the Authorization Detail screen for the first time without any prior session context, by checking if a communication area exists from a previous interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined this is a new session with no prior session data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The new session redirect workflow is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire CardDemo communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is initialized to its default empty state, clearing all fields including account ID, customer ID, program context, and any previously selected authorization data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Fresh Communication Area for New Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new session is detected, the system initializes a clean communication area to ensure no stale or residual data from any prior session is carried forward into the redirect process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new session has been detected and the communication area has been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redirect the user away from the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program in the communication area (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is set to the Authorization Summary program (WS-PGM-AUTH-SMRY), directing the user to the summary list screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Redirect Destination to Authorization Summary Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new session is detected on the Authorization Detail screen, the system sets the target destination program to the Authorization Summary screen, as the user must first select an authorization from the summary before viewing its details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redirect the user to the Authorization Summary screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-CICS-TRANID) is recorded in the communication area field CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, and the Authorization Detail program name (WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL) is recorded in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, establishing the Authorization Detail screen as the originating screen for navigation tracking

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Authorization Detail Screen as the Originating Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redirecting the user, the system records the Authorization Detail screen's transaction ID and program name as the originating screen in the communication area, so the destination screen knows where the navigation came from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The originating screen information has been recorded in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the redirect preparation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program context field (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is set to zeros (no context), and the program entry state flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is set to TRUE, indicating a fresh first-time entry to the destination program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Program Context to Fresh Entry State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redirecting the user, the system resets the program context indicators to represent a clean, first-time entry state, ensuring the destination Authorization Summary screen treats this as a fresh navigation rather than a return from a sub-screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The communication area has been initialized, the destination is set to Authorization Summary, the originating screen is recorded, and the program context is reset to fresh entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The redirect is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is immediately transferred (via XCTL) to the Authorization Summary program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) with the prepared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) passed along, and the Authorization Detail screen is not displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect User to Authorization Summary Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all redirect preparation steps are complete, the system transfers control to the Authorization Summary screen, passing the initialized communication area, so the user can select an authorization record before accessing its details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has navigated to the Authorization Detail screen for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the Account ID is numeric AND the Selected Authorization Key is not blank and not low-values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If both conditions are met, the system proceeds to read the authorization records using the Account ID and Authorization Key; if either condition fails, an error flag is set and no authorization data is displayed on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Account ID and Authorization Selection Before Loading Detail
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading any authorization records, the system must verify that a valid numeric Account ID exists and that a specific authorization has been selected. If either condition fails, no data is loaded and an error state is set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID and Authorization Key have been validated as present and valid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve the Authorization Summary record from the Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the summary record is found, the system proceeds to read the Authorization Detail record; if the summary record is not found or the end of the database is reached, an error flag is set and no authorization data is displayed on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Authorization Summary Record by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system retrieves the Authorization Summary record from the database using the Account ID as the key. If the summary record is not found, an error state is set and no detail data is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Summary record has been successfully retrieved for the given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve the Authorization Detail record from the Pending Authorization Detail segment (PAUTDTL1) using the Selected Authorization Key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the detail record is found, the system proceeds to format and display the authorization details; if the detail record is not found or the end of the database is reached, an error flag is set and no authorization data is displayed on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Authorization Detail Record by Authorization Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the Authorization Summary, the system retrieves the specific Authorization Detail record using the Authorization Key. If the detail record is not found, an error state is set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully retrieved and the error flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the authorization origination date for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization origination date stored as YYMMDD is reformatted so that characters 1-2 (YY) map to the year portion, characters 3-4 (MM) map to the month portion, and characters 5-6 (DD) map to the day portion, resulting in a display date in MM/DD/YY format shown in the Authorization Date field (AUTHDTO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Authorization Origination Date for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization origination date stored in the system in YYMMDD format must be reformatted into MM/DD/YY format before being displayed on the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully retrieved and the error flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the authorization origination time for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization origination time is formatted by placing characters 1-2 (HH) into positions 1-2 of the display time field, characters 3-4 (MM) into positions 4-5, and characters 5-6 (SS) into positions 7-8, with colon separators at positions 3 and 6, resulting in HH:MM:SS format shown in the Authorization Time field (AUTHTMO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Authorization Origination Time for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization origination time stored in the system must be formatted with colon separators (HH:MM:SS) before being displayed on the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully retrieved and the error flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the card expiry date for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card expiry date is formatted by placing characters 1-2 (MM) into positions 1-2 of the display field, a literal '/' into position 3, and characters 3-4 (YY) into positions 4-5, resulting in MM/YY format shown in the Card Expiry Date field (CRDEXPO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Card Expiry Date with Slash Separator
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card expiry date stored in the system must be formatted with a slash separator (MM/YY) before being displayed on the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully retrieved and the error flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Authorization Response Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the response code is '00', the Authorization Status field (AUTHRSPO) is set to 'A' (Approved) and displayed in GREEN; if the response code is any value other than '00', the Authorization Status field (AUTHRSPO) is set to 'D' (Declined) and displayed in RED

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Authorization Approval or Decline Status and Color
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization response code determines whether the transaction was approved or declined, and the screen must display the status with a corresponding color indicator to visually distinguish approved from declined authorizations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully retrieved and the error flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the Decline Reason Table for a matching entry where the decline code equals the Authorization Response Reason code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a matching entry is found, the Authorization Reason field (AUTHRSNO) is populated with the response reason code followed by a '-' separator and the corresponding decline description from the table; if no matching entry is found, the Authorization Reason field (AUTHRSNO) is populated with '9999' followed by '-' and 'ERROR' to indicate an unrecognized decline reason

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lookup and Display Decline Reason Description from Reason Code Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization response reason code must be looked up in the predefined Decline Reason table to retrieve a human-readable description. If the reason code is not found in the table, a default error indicator is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully retrieved and the error flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the fraud status of the authorization record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the authorization fraud status is Confirmed OR Removed (indicating the authorization has a fraud history), the Fraud Status field (AUTHFRDO) is populated with the fraud flag indicator in position 1, a '-' separator in position 2, and the Fraud Report Date starting at position 3; if the authorization has no fraud history (neither confirmed nor removed), the Fraud Status field (AUTHFRDO) is populated with only a '-'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Fraud Status Flag and Report Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fraud status field on the Authorization Detail screen must reflect whether the authorization has any fraud history, displaying the fraud flag and report date when applicable, or a dash when no fraud history exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully retrieved and the error flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the remaining fields on the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following fields are populated directly from the Authorization Detail record: Card Number (CARDNUMO), Approved Amount (AUTHAMTO), Processing Code (AUTHCDO), POS Entry Mode (POSEMDO), Message Source (AUTHSRCO), Merchant Category Code (MCCCDO), Authorization Type (AUTHTYPO), Transaction ID (TRNIDO), Match Status (AUTHMTCO), Merchant Name (MERNAMEO), Merchant ID (MERIDO), Merchant City (MERCITYO), Merchant State (MERSTO), and Merchant Zip (MERZIPO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Remaining Authorization Detail Fields on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: All remaining authorization and merchant detail fields must be populated on the Authorization Detail screen from the retrieved authorization record when no error condition exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail screen is about to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title Line 1 (TITLE01O) from the application title constant, Application Title Line 2 (TITLE02O) from the application title constant, Transaction Name (TRNNAMEO) from the current CICS transaction ID, Program Name (PGMNAMEO) set to the Authorization Detail program name, Current Date (CURDATEO) formatted as MM/DD/YY from the current system date, and Current Time (CURTIMEO) formatted as HH:MM:SS from the current system time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time, and Program Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Authorization Detail screen is displayed, the screen header must be refreshed with the current system date and time, along with the application title, transaction name, and program name.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail screen data has been fully populated and the screen send flag is set to ERASE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A from mapset COPAU01) to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is displayed with a full ERASE, clearing all previously displayed content, and the cursor is positioned at the Card Number field (CARDNUML set to -1), ensuring the user sees a completely refreshed Authorization Detail screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Authorization Detail Screen with Full Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: On first entry to the Authorization Detail screen, the screen must be sent with a full erase to ensure a clean display, clearing any previously displayed data before showing the current authorization details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen with a valid Account ID (numeric) and a pending authorization record selected (not spaces or low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the authorization record for the selected Account ID and Authorization Key, populates all authorization detail fields on the screen (card number, authorization date, authorization time, approved amount, response status, decline reason, processing code, POS entry mode, message source, merchant category code, card expiry date, authorization type, transaction ID, match status, fraud status, merchant details), and redisplays the Authorization Detail screen with the refreshed data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enter Key Triggers Authorization Detail Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key on the Authorization Detail screen, the system re-processes and refreshes the currently selected authorization record details and redisplays the updated Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key AND either the Account ID is not numeric OR no authorization record is selected (value is spaces or low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error flag ON, skips population of all authorization detail fields, and redisplays the Authorization Detail screen without authorization data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enter Key with Missing or Invalid Selection Sets Error State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key but either the Account ID is not numeric or no authorization record has been selected, the system sets an error condition and does not populate authorization detail fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Authorization Summary program, records the current transaction ID and Authorization Detail program name as the originating context, resets the program context to initial entry state, and transfers control to the Authorization Summary screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF3 Key Returns User to Authorization Summary Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Authorization Detail screen, the system navigates the user back to the Authorization Summary screen, preserving the session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen with a pending authorization record currently displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF5 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs fraud mark or removal processing on the current authorization record and redisplays the Authorization Detail screen reflecting the updated fraud status and a confirmation or error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF5 Key Invokes Fraud Mark or Removal Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF5 on the Authorization Detail screen, the system toggles the fraud status of the currently displayed authorization — confirming it as fraud if not already flagged, or removing the fraud flag if already confirmed — and redisplays the updated Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen viewing a pending authorization record for a specific account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF8 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the current authorization record, then reads the next sequential authorization record for the same account; if a next record exists, the system updates the selected authorization to the next record and displays its full details on the Authorization Detail screen; if no next record exists (end of list), the system displays the message 'Already at the last Authorization...' and refreshes the screen without erasing the currently displayed authorization data

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF8 Key Navigates to Next Authorization Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 on the Authorization Detail screen, the system advances to the next pending authorization record for the same account and displays its details, or informs the user if no further records exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key that is not Enter, PF3, PF5, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system re-processes the current authorization data (same as Enter key behavior), sets the screen message to the standard 'Invalid Key' message text, and redisplays the Authorization Detail screen with the invalid key notification — no authorization data is changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unrecognized Key Press Displays Invalid Key Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF5, or PF8 on the Authorization Detail screen, the system displays an invalid key message and refreshes the screen without changing any authorization data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing for a key press (Enter, PF5, PF8, or any other key — excluding PF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Authorization Detail screen is about to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with the current system date (MM/DD/YY format) and current system time (HH:MM:SS format), along with the application title, transaction name, and program name; any message (error, confirmation, or invalid key) is placed in the message field; the cursor is positioned on the card number field; and the screen is displayed — using full screen erase if the erase flag is set to YES, or without erase if set to NO (e.g., when already at last authorization)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Screen Redisplayed After Key Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After processing any key action (Enter, PF5, PF8, or Other), the system always refreshes and redisplays the Authorization Detail screen with updated header information including current system date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Authorization Detail screen and has an active session with valid communication area data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Authorization Summary program (WS-PGM-AUTH-SMRY) as the destination program in the communication area (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), indicating where control should be transferred

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Authorization Summary as Navigation Destination on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Authorization Detail screen, the system designates the Authorization Summary screen as the target destination for navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 and the destination has been set to the Authorization Summary screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the Authorization Summary screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the current CICS Transaction ID (WS-CICS-TRANID) into the communication area field CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, preserving the originating transaction identity for the receiving screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Originating Transaction ID Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before navigating away from the Authorization Detail screen, the system records the current transaction identifier so the destination screen knows which transaction initiated the navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to navigate back to the Authorization Summary screen after PF3 was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the navigation context in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the current Authorization Detail program name (WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL) into the communication area field CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, identifying the Authorization Detail screen as the originating program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Originating Program Name Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control, the system records the name of the current Authorization Detail program so the Authorization Summary screen can identify which program initiated the navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to transfer control to the Authorization Summary screen after PF3 was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the navigation context in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zeros AND sets the program entry state flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) to TRUE, ensuring the Authorization Summary screen initializes as a fresh entry with no prior state carried over

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Program Context to Fresh Entry State Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the Authorization Summary screen, the system resets the program context so the destination screen treats the incoming navigation as a fresh entry rather than a re-entry, ensuring a clean initial display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been set to Authorization Summary, the originating transaction ID and program name have been recorded, and the program context has been reset to fresh entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control (XCTL) to the Authorization Summary program identified in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, passing the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing the originating transaction ID, originating program name, and fresh entry state — resulting in the Authorization Summary screen being displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Authorization Summary Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After preparing all navigation context data, the system transfers full control to the Authorization Summary screen, passing the complete session communication area so the destination screen has all necessary context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is viewing an authorization detail record on the Authorization Detail screen and presses PF5
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the current authorization record and evaluates its fraud status flag
