Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system commits the transaction (SYNCPOINT), permanently persisting the fraud status change to the Authorization Detail record in the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Transaction on Successful Authorization Detail Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Authorization Detail record is successfully saved to the database, the system must commit the transaction to make the fraud status change permanent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully updated and committed to the database, and the fraud action performed was the removal of a previously confirmed fraud flag (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines which success message to display based on the type of fraud action performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...' to the user, confirming that the fraud flag has been successfully removed from the authorization

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Message When Fraud Flag Is Removed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful database commit, if the fraud action was a removal of a previously confirmed fraud flag, the system must display a specific confirmation message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail record has been successfully updated and committed to the database, and the fraud action performed was confirming the authorization as fraudulent (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED is false, meaning PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED was set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines which success message to display based on the type of fraud action performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...' to the user, confirming that the authorization has been successfully flagged as fraudulent

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Message When Authorization Is Marked as Fraud
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful database commit, if the fraud action was a confirmation of fraud on the authorization, the system must display a specific confirmation message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system attempted to save the updated Authorization Detail record to the database, and the database update operation returned a non-successful status (status is not OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that the database update has failed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system rolls back the entire transaction (SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK) to undo any changes made during this operation, sets the error flag to 'Y', and displays a system error message indicating that the fraud tagging operation failed along with the database error status code, then refreshes the Authorization Detail screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Rollback Transaction and Display Error When Database Update Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Authorization Detail record cannot be successfully saved to the database, the system must rollback the entire transaction to prevent partial or inconsistent data, and display an error message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external fraud management program (WS-PGM-AUTH-FRAUD) has been called and returned a normal CICS response, meaning the program executed without a system-level failure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the fraud program's business-level update result (WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the fraud program reports a successful update (WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS is true), the system proceeds to update the Authorization Detail record in the database; if the fraud program reports an unsuccessful update (WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS is false), the system displays the fraud program's action message (WS-FRD-ACT-MSG) to the user and rolls back the transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Fraud Update Outcome Based on External Fraud Program Response
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the external fraud program is called, the system must evaluate the fraud program's update result to determine whether to proceed with saving the authorization detail or to rollback and display the fraud program's error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fraud mark or fraud removal action has been completed (either successfully committed or rolled back), and the authorization key is available from the Pending Authorization Detail record (PA-AUTHORIZATION-KEY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to return the updated view to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the currently selected authorization key (CDEMO-CPVD-PAU-SELECTED) to the authorization key from the Pending Authorization Detail record (PA-AUTHORIZATION-KEY), then populates and refreshes the Authorization Detail screen with all current authorization fields including the updated fraud status, displaying the current fraud flag and fraud report date if fraud has been confirmed or removed, or a '-' if no fraud history exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Refresh Authorization Detail Screen After Fraud Action Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After any fraud action (successful or failed), the system must refresh the Authorization Detail screen with the current state of the authorization record so the user sees the latest fraud status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been submitted to the external Fraud Management program to either confirm or remove a fraud flag
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The external Fraud Management program returns a response to the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Fraud Management program completed successfully, the system proceeds to check whether the fraud data update itself was successful; if the program did not complete successfully (call failure), the system immediately rolls back all pending database changes without displaying any fraud program error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate Fraud Program Execution Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external Fraud Management program is called to mark or unmark an authorization as fraud, the system must evaluate whether the program completed its execution without failure before proceeding with any database updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external Fraud Management program has completed its execution successfully and returned a response
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the fraud update success indicator returned by the Fraud Management program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the fraud update was successful, the system proceeds to commit the authorization record update to the database; if the fraud update was not successful, the system captures the error message returned by the Fraud Management program, rolls back all pending database changes, and displays the captured error message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate Fraud Data Update Result from Fraud Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming the external Fraud Management program completed successfully, the system must further evaluate whether the fraud data update operation within that program was actually successful before committing any changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external Fraud Management program has completed execution but reported that the fraud data update was not successful
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the unsuccessful fraud update response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the action error message (WS-FRD-ACT-MSG) returned by the Fraud Management program and stores it as the current screen message to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Fraud Program Error Message on Update Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external Fraud Management program reports that the fraud data update was unsuccessful, the system must capture the specific error message returned by the fraud program so it can be communicated to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external Fraud Management program completed execution but returned an unsuccessful fraud update result, and the fraud program's error message has been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the fraud update failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs a full rollback of all pending database changes, ensuring no partial fraud status updates are committed to the authorization record, and then displays the fraud program's error message to the user on the Authorization Detail screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Rollback Database Changes on Fraud Update Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external Fraud Management program reports that the fraud data update was unsuccessful, all pending database changes related to the fraud marking or unmarking operation must be undone to preserve data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record's fraud status change has been initiated and submitted to the external Fraud Management program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The external Fraud Management program fails to complete its execution (the program call itself does not return a normal response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs a full rollback of all pending database changes immediately, no fraud program error message is displayed (since none was returned), and the system continues to refresh the Authorization Detail screen in its pre-update state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Rollback Database Changes on Fraud Program Call Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external Fraud Management program itself fails to execute (program call failure), all pending database changes must be immediately rolled back without any error message from the fraud program, since no response was received.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The fraud data update has failed, the fraud program's error message has been captured, and the database rollback has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Authorization Detail screen is refreshed after the failed fraud operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message returned by the Fraud Management program is displayed in the message area of the Authorization Detail screen, the screen header is refreshed with the current date and time, and the authorization details remain visible so the user can review the current state of the record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Fraud Update Error Message to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After rolling back database changes due to a fraud update failure, the system must display the error message received from the Fraud Management program to inform the user why the fraud marking or unmarking operation could not be completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fraud status toggle action (mark or remove fraud) has been processed for a selected authorization record, and the fraud processing workspace (WS-FRAUD-AUTH-RECORD) contains the updated authorization details including the new fraud status flag and fraud report date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to persist the fraud status change to the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the complete updated authorization detail record from the fraud processing workspace into the pending authorization detail record, ensuring the new fraud status and fraud report date are included before the database save is attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Updated Authorization Detail Record with Fraud Status
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving to the database, the system prepares the authorization detail record by applying the updated fraud status and fraud report date from the fraud processing workspace into the pending authorization detail record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The pending authorization detail record has been prepared with the updated fraud status and fraud report date, and the authorization detail segment (PAUTDTL1) exists in the database under the correct account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to replace the existing authorization detail record in the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must overwrite the existing authorization detail record with the updated record containing the new fraud status; the outcome of the save operation (success or failure) must be captured to determine the next processing step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Updated Authorization Detail Record to Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system replaces the existing authorization detail record in the database with the updated record containing the new fraud status and report date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The updated authorization detail record with the new fraud status and report date has been successfully saved to the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database save operation completes with a successful status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately commit (take a syncpoint) to make all database changes permanent, ensuring the fraud status update is durably recorded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Transaction on Successful Authorization Detail Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the authorization detail record is successfully saved to the database, the system must commit the transaction to make all changes permanent and irreversible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization detail record has been successfully saved and the transaction has been committed, and the fraud action performed was a removal of a previously confirmed fraud flag (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the type of fraud action that was completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...' to confirm to the user that the fraud flag has been successfully removed from the authorization record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Fraud Removal Confirmation Message After Successful Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful database save and commit, if the fraud flag was being removed from the authorization, the system displays a specific confirmation message to inform the user that the fraud marking has been reversed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization detail record has been successfully saved and the transaction has been committed, and the fraud action performed was a confirmation of fraud (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED is false, meaning fraud was confirmed/added)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the type of fraud action that was completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...' to confirm to the user that the authorization record has been successfully flagged as fraudulent

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Fraud Confirmation Message After Successful Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful database save and commit, if the fraud flag was being added to the authorization, the system displays a specific confirmation message to inform the user that the authorization has been successfully marked as fraudulent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system attempted to save the updated authorization detail record with the new fraud status to the database, and the save operation did not complete successfully (any status other than success)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database save operation returns a failure status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately rollback the transaction (SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK) to undo all database changes made during this transaction, ensuring no partial or inconsistent fraud status updates are persisted to the authorization record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Rollback Transaction on Failed Authorization Detail Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the database save of the updated authorization detail record fails for any reason, the system must rollback the entire transaction to undo all changes and preserve data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization detail record has been successfully updated in the database with the new fraud status (either fraud confirmed or fraud removed), and the database update operation returned a successful status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the successful database update result for the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately commit all pending database changes to make them permanent and irreversible, ensuring the fraud status update is durably recorded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Database Changes After Successful Authorization Fraud Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization detail record has been successfully updated in the database (either marking or removing a fraud flag), all pending database changes must be permanently committed to ensure data integrity and consistency.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization detail record has been successfully updated in the database and all changes have been committed, AND the action performed was the removal of a previously confirmed fraud flag (fraud flag was toggled from confirmed to removed)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the type of fraud action that was committed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set and display the success message 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...' to confirm to the user that the fraud flag has been successfully removed from the authorization record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Fraud Removal Success Confirmation Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful database commit following a fraud flag removal action, the system must inform the user that the fraud marking has been successfully removed from the authorization record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization detail record has been successfully updated in the database and all changes have been committed, AND the action performed was the confirmation of fraud (fraud flag was toggled from not-confirmed to confirmed)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the type of fraud action that was committed and determines that the fraud flag was NOT removed (i.e., it was added/confirmed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set and display the success message 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...' to confirm to the user that the authorization record has been successfully flagged as fraudulent

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Fraud Confirmation Success Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful database commit following a fraud flag confirmation action, the system must inform the user that the authorization record has been successfully marked as fraudulent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has requested to mark or unmark an authorization as fraudulent, and the authorization detail record, account ID (WS-FRD-ACCT-ID), and customer ID (WS-FRD-CUST-ID) have been populated in the fraud data communication area (WS-FRAUD-DATA)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the external Fraud Management program (WS-PGM-AUTH-FRAUD) via a program link, passing the fraud data communication area containing the full authorization detail record, account ID, and customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The external Fraud Management program is called and the system waits for a response before proceeding with any database update or rollback action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke External Fraud Management Program to Process Fraud Status Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a fraud status toggle is initiated for an authorization record, the system must invoke the external Fraud Management program, passing the authorization details, account ID, and customer ID, before any database changes are committed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fraud status toggle has been initiated for an authorization record and the external Fraud Management program has been invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program link to the external Fraud Management program returns a non-normal response (i.e., the call itself fails, not a business-level failure)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately initiates a rollback of all database changes for the current transaction, ensuring no partial updates are saved, and displays an error message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Rollback All Changes When External Fraud Program Call Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system is unable to successfully communicate with the external Fraud Management program (i.e., the program link itself fails), all pending changes for the transaction must be rolled back immediately without any database update being applied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external Fraud Management program was successfully invoked (program link succeeded) and has returned a response
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fraud program indicates that the fraud update was NOT successful (WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS is false), and the fraud program has returned an action message (WS-FRD-ACT-MSG)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the error message returned by the fraud program (WS-FRD-ACT-MSG) into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), initiates a rollback of all database changes, and displays the captured fraud program error message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Fraud Program Business Failure Message Before Rollback
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external Fraud Management program is successfully called but reports that the fraud update was not successful at the business level, the system must capture the error message returned by the fraud program and display it to the user after rolling back all changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external Fraud Management program was successfully invoked (program link returned normal response)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fraud program confirms a successful update (WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to update the authorization detail record (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS) in the database with the fraud-tagged data from WS-FRAUD-AUTH-RECORD

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Database Update When Fraud Program Confirms Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the external Fraud Management program is successfully called and confirms that the fraud status update was processed successfully, the system proceeds to update the authorization detail record in the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The fraud program confirmed success and the system has attempted to update the authorization detail record (PAUTDTL1 segment) in the database with the fraud-tagged data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database update operation completes successfully (status is OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system commits all changes via a syncpoint, and displays either 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...' if the fraud flag was being removed (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED is true), or 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...' if the authorization was being confirmed as fraudulent (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED is true)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Changes and Confirm Fraud Status Update When Database Update Succeeds
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the authorization detail record is successfully updated in the database with the new fraud status, the system commits the transaction and displays a confirmation message indicating whether fraud was marked or removed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The fraud program confirmed success and the system has attempted to update the authorization detail record in the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database update operation fails (status is not OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs an error message containing the text 'System error while FRAUD Tagging, ROLLBACK' concatenated with the database return code, stores it in WS-MESSAGE, initiates a rollback of all database changes, and displays the error message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture System Error Message When Database Update Fails During Fraud Tagging
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database update of the authorization detail record fails during fraud tagging, the system must capture a descriptive system error message indicating the failure context before initiating a rollback.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fraud status update has been attempted and a failure has occurred at any stage: the program link to the fraud management program failed, the fraud program reported an unsuccessful update, or the database record update failed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates a rollback
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All database changes made during the current transaction are fully reversed via a CICS Syncpoint Rollback, ensuring no partial or inconsistent fraud data is saved to the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Rollback All Database Changes to Preserve Data Integrity on Any Fraud Update Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Whenever any failure occurs during the fraud status update process — whether the fraud program call failed, the fraud program reported a business failure, or the database update failed — all database changes made during the current transaction must be fully rolled back to ensure data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A rollback has been executed due to a failure in the fraud status update process (either fraud program link failure, fraud program business failure, or database update failure), and an error message has been captured in WS-MESSAGE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The rollback completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the Authorization Detail screen (COPAU1A from mapset COPAU01) to the user with the error message displayed in the ERRMSGO field, and the screen header is refreshed with the current date and time, so the user is informed that the fraud update failed and no changes were saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Message to User After Rollback
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a rollback is executed due to any fraud update failure, the system must display the relevant error message to the user on the Authorization Detail screen, informing them that no changes were saved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail screen is about to be displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores them in the working date and time data fields (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent use in formatting and displaying on the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time to ensure the header reflects real-time information each time the Authorization Detail screen is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Application title lines are being set on the Authorization Detail screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the first application title line (CCDA-TITLE01) into the screen header Title Line 1 field (TITLE01O) and the second application title line (CCDA-TITLE02) into the screen header Title Line 2 field (TITLE02O)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Application Title Lines on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display two standard application title lines sourced from the centrally maintained application title definitions, ensuring consistent branding across all screens.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction identifier is being set on the Authorization Detail screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the current CICS transaction ID (WS-CICS-TRANID) into the Transaction Name field (TRNNAMEO) on the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the active CICS transaction identifier so users and support staff can identify which transaction is currently running.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name is being set on the Authorization Detail screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the Authorization Detail program name (WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL) into the Program Name field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the name of the currently executing program (Authorization Detail program) to provide context to users and support staff.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in working date fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The date is being formatted for display on the Authorization Detail screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) into the MM position (WS-CURDATE-MM), the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) into the DD position (WS-CURDATE-DD), and the last two digits of the year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR positions 3-4) into the YY position (WS-CURDATE-YY), composing the date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Date into MM/DD/YY for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date must be reformatted from its raw system format into the standard MM/DD/YY display format before being shown on the screen header, ensuring date readability for business users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format and stored in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The formatted date is being applied to the Authorization Detail screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the MM/DD/YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) into the Current Date display field (CURDATEO) on the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Formatted Date on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format, it must be placed into the designated date field on the screen header so users can see the current date when viewing the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored in working time fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The time is being formatted for display on the Authorization Detail screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) into the HH position (WS-CURTIME-HH), the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) into the MM position (WS-CURTIME-MM), and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) into the SS position (WS-CURTIME-SS), composing the time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Time into HH:MM:SS for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system time must be reformatted from its raw system format into the standard HH:MM:SS display format before being shown on the screen header, ensuring time readability for business users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format and stored in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The formatted time is being applied to the Authorization Detail screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the HH:MM:SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) into the Current Time display field (CURTIMEO) on the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Formatted Time on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format, it must be placed into the designated time field on the screen header so users can see the current time when viewing the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to send the Authorization Detail screen (COPAU1A / COPAU01) to the user terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine (POPULATE-HEADER-INFO) is executed prior to sending the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header must be populated with: (1) Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) displayed in TITLE01O field, (2) Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) displayed in TITLE02O field, (3) Current CICS Transaction ID (WS-CICS-TRANID) displayed in TRNNAMEO field, (4) Current Program Name (WS-PGM-AUTH-DTL) displayed in PGMNAMEO field, (5) Current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY displayed in CURDATEO field, (6) Current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS displayed in CURTIMEO field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current System Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Authorization Detail screen, the system populates the screen header with application titles, the current transaction identifier, the program name, and the current system date and time to provide context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing of a user action (Enter, PF5, PF8, or invalid key) and may have generated a business message in WS-MESSAGE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Authorization Detail screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The content of WS-MESSAGE is moved to the ERRMSGO field of the screen map (COPAU1AO), ensuring any message such as 'AUTH MARKED FRAUD...', 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...', 'Already at the last Authorization...', or 'Invalid Key' is visible to the user in the designated message area of the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Business Message in Screen Message Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any business message generated during processing (such as validation errors, fraud action confirmations, navigation limit notifications, or invalid key warnings) must be placed in the screen message area before the Authorization Detail screen is sent to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is ready to send the Authorization Detail screen after processing a user action
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen send routine evaluates the SEND-ERASE flag (SEND-ERASE-YES or SEND-ERASE-NO)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If SEND-ERASE-YES is active, the system performs a full screen erase before display; if SEND-ERASE-NO is active, the system performs a partial screen refresh without erasing existing content. The default state at the start of every transaction cycle is SEND-ERASE-YES, meaning full erase is the default behavior unless explicitly overridden

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Screen Refresh Mode: Full Erase or Partial Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system determines whether to send the Authorization Detail screen with a full erase (clearing the entire terminal screen before display) or a partial refresh (updating the screen without clearing it), based on the navigation context of the current action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SEND-ERASE flag is set to SEND-ERASE-YES (which is the default set at the beginning of each transaction cycle in MAIN-PARA), applicable during: initial screen display, Enter key processing, PF5 fraud mark/unmark actions, and any invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the SEND-AUTHVIEW-SCREEN routine and evaluates the SEND-ERASE flag as SEND-ERASE-YES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A from mapset COPAU01) to the terminal using the ERASE option, which clears the entire terminal screen before rendering the updated screen content, and positions the cursor at the Card Number field (CARDNUML set to -1)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Authorization Detail Screen with Full Erase
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Authorization Detail screen is sent to the user terminal with a full screen erase as the default behavior, applied during initial screen load, Enter key processing, PF5 fraud toggle actions, and all standard navigation scenarios.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user pressed PF8 to navigate to the next authorization record, and the system determined that there are no more authorization records available (AUTHS-EOF condition is true, meaning the end of the authorization list has been reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The PROCESS-PF8-KEY routine sets SEND-ERASE-NO (overriding the default SEND-ERASE-YES) and the SEND-AUTHVIEW-SCREEN routine evaluates the SEND-ERASE flag as SEND-ERASE-NO
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A from mapset COPAU01) to the terminal WITHOUT the ERASE option, meaning the existing screen content is not cleared before the update, the current authorization details remain visible, and the message 'Already at the last Authorization...' is displayed in the screen message area (ERRMSGO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Authorization Detail Screen with Partial Refresh When at Last Authorization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to navigate forward (PF8) but has already reached the last authorization record for the account, the screen is refreshed without a full erase, preserving the currently displayed authorization details while showing the end-of-list notification message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF8 to navigate to the next authorization record for the current account, and the system has attempted to read the next authorization detail record from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read of the next authorization record results in an end-of-data condition (AUTHS-EOF is set to TRUE, indicating no further authorization records exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets SEND-ERASE-NO to TRUE (overriding the default SEND-ERASE-YES), and sets WS-MESSAGE to 'Already at the last Authorization...' to notify the user that forward navigation is not possible; the currently displayed authorization record remains unchanged on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Partial Refresh Flag When End of Authorization List is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: During forward navigation (PF8), when the system detects that no further authorization records exist for the account, it overrides the default full-erase screen send behavior by setting the partial refresh flag and prepares the end-of-list notification message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user session is active with a valid communication area (session data is present), and the Authorization Detail screen processing is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the program re-entry indicator (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) in the session communication area to determine if the Authorization Detail screen has already been displayed to the user in this session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the re-entry indicator shows this is NOT a re-entry (first time display), the system marks the session as re-entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE) and routes to the first-time display path; If the re-entry indicator shows this IS a re-entry (screen was already displayed), the system routes to the screen input receipt path to accept user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Screen Re-Entry Status for Authorization Detail Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system evaluates whether the Authorization Detail screen has been previously displayed to the user in the current session. This determination controls whether the system should accept new user input or load and display fresh authorization data for the first time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user session is active with valid session data, and the program re-entry indicator (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to FALSE indicating the Authorization Detail screen has not yet been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects this is the first time the Authorization Detail screen is being presented to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips the screen input receipt step entirely, marks the session as re-entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE to flag future visits as re-entries), proceeds directly to load the authorization record data using the account ID and selected authorization key from the session, and sends the populated Authorization Detail screen to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Bypass Input Receipt on First-Time Authorization Detail Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Authorization Detail screen is being displayed for the first time in a session, the system bypasses the user input receipt step and instead directly loads and displays the authorization data. No user input is expected or collected on the initial screen display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A within mapset COPAU01) has been previously displayed to the user, and the program re-entry indicator (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is TRUE indicating a re-entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits input by pressing any key on the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system accepts and captures all user input from the Authorization Detail screen into the screen input data area (COPAU1AI), making all submitted field values and keystrokes available for subsequent processing and keystroke evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept User Input from Authorization Detail Screen on Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has already been presented with the Authorization Detail screen and submits input (by pressing a key), the system must collect all data entered or selected by the user from the screen before processing any actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted input on the Authorization Detail screen (map COPAU1A, mapset COPAU01) and the system has initiated the input receipt process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen data from the Authorization Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All screen field values entered or displayed on the Authorization Detail screen are captured into the input map data area (COPAU1AI), and the specific attention identifier (the key pressed by the user, such as ENTER, PF3, PF5, PF8, or any other key) is recorded and made available for keystroke evaluation to determine the next business action to perform

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture All Screen Fields Including User Keystrokes and Selections
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system captures the complete set of screen fields submitted by the user, including all data fields and the specific attention key (function key or Enter) pressed. This captured data forms the basis for all subsequent business processing decisions such as fraud marking, navigation, or data refresh.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original date stored in YYMMDD format in the Authorization Original Date field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization date for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first two characters (positions 1-2) of the Authorization Original Date field, representing the Year (YY), are extracted and placed into the Year component of the display date working field (WS-CURDATE-YY)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Year Component from Authorization Original Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization original date is stored in YYMMDD format. The year component occupies the first two characters and must be extracted separately before the date can be reformatted for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original date stored in YYMMDD format in the Authorization Original Date field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization date for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Characters at positions 3-4 of the Authorization Original Date field, representing the Month (MM), are extracted and placed into the Month component of the display date working field (WS-CURDATE-MM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Month Component from Authorization Original Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization original date is stored in YYMMDD format. The month component occupies characters 3 and 4 and must be extracted separately before the date can be reformatted for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original date stored in YYMMDD format in the Authorization Original Date field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization date for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Characters at positions 5-6 of the Authorization Original Date field, representing the Day (DD), are extracted and placed into the Day component of the display date working field (WS-CURDATE-DD)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Day Component from Authorization Original Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization original date is stored in YYMMDD format. The day component occupies characters 5 and 6 and must be extracted separately before the date can be reformatted for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Year (WS-CURDATE-YY), Month (WS-CURDATE-MM), and Day (WS-CURDATE-DD) components have been individually extracted from the Authorization Original Date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the date for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The three extracted components are combined into the MM/DD/YY display format and stored in the authorization date display working field (WS-AUTH-DATE), where Month appears first, followed by Day, followed by Year, with slash separators

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reassemble Authorization Date into MM/DD/YY Display Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: After extracting the individual year, month, and day components from the YYMMDD stored format, the system reassembles them into the MM/DD/YY display format required for the authorization detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization date has been successfully reformatted into MM/DD/YY format and stored in the authorization date display working field (WS-AUTH-DATE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Authorization Detail screen fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted MM/DD/YY authorization date is moved to the screen Authorization Date output field (AUTHDTO) for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Move Formatted Authorization Date to Screen Display Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the authorization date has been reformatted into MM/DD/YY format, it must be transferred to the screen output field so it is visible to the user on the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original time stored in HHMMSS format in the Authorization Original Time field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization time for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first two characters (positions 1-2) of the Authorization Original Time field, representing Hours (HH), are placed into positions 1-2 of the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME), which will form the HH portion of the HH:MM:SS display format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract and Place Hours Component into Time Display Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization original time is stored in HHMMSS format. The hours component (positions 1-2) must be extracted and placed into the first two positions of the formatted time display field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original time stored in HHMMSS format, and the Hours component has already been placed into positions 1-2 of the time display working field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization time for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Characters at positions 3-4 of the Authorization Original Time field, representing Minutes (MM), are placed into positions 4-5 of the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME), leaving position 3 as a colon separator between Hours and Minutes in the resulting HH:MM:SS format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract and Place Minutes Component into Time Display Field with Colon Separator
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization original time is stored in HHMMSS format. The minutes component (positions 3-4 of source) must be placed into positions 4-5 of the display field, with a colon separator implicitly occupying position 3 of the display field between hours and minutes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record exists with an original time stored in HHMMSS format, and the Hours and Minutes components have already been placed into the time display working field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization time for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Characters at positions 5-6 of the Authorization Original Time field, representing Seconds (SS), are placed into positions 7-8 of the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME), leaving position 6 as a colon separator between Minutes and Seconds, completing the HH:MM:SS display format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract and Place Seconds Component into Time Display Field with Colon Separator
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization original time is stored in HHMMSS format. The seconds component (positions 5-6 of source) must be placed into positions 7-8 of the display field, with a colon separator implicitly occupying position 6 of the display field between minutes and seconds.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization time has been successfully assembled into HH:MM:SS format with colon separators at positions 3 and 6, stored in the time display working field (WS-AUTH-TIME)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Authorization Detail screen fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fully formatted HH:MM:SS authorization time is moved to the screen Authorization Time output field (AUTHTMO) for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Move Formatted Authorization Time to Screen Display Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the authorization time has been fully assembled into HH:MM:SS format with colon separators, it must be transferred to the screen output field so it is visible to the user on the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record has been successfully retrieved and contains a Card Expiry Date stored in 4-character MMYY format (where the first 2 characters represent the month and the last 2 characters represent the year), and the error flag is not set (authorization details are eligible for display)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the authorization detail screen with the card expiry date field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Extract the first 2 characters of the stored Card Expiry Date as the Month portion and place them in display positions 1-2 of the Card Expiry Date display field (CRDEXPO); (2) Insert a forward slash '/' character as the 3rd character of the Card Expiry Date display field (CRDEXPO) as a separator; (3) Extract the last 2 characters of the stored Card Expiry Date as the Year portion and place them in display positions 4-5 of the Card Expiry Date display field (CRDEXPO); resulting in the Card Expiry Date being displayed on screen in MM/YY format (e.g., a stored value of '1226' is displayed as '12/26')

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Card Expiry Date for Display in MM/YY Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: When displaying authorization details on screen, the card expiry date stored in the system in MMYY format must be reformatted into a human-readable MM/YY display format by extracting the month and year portions separately and inserting a slash separator between them.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Account ID is available in the current session and an Authorization Key (selected authorization) has been identified for retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates a search for the Authorization Summary record using the Account ID as the primary search key against the Authorization Summary data store (PAUTSUM0)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Authorization Summary record matching the provided Account ID and proceeds to evaluate whether the record was found, not found, or the end of available records has been reached

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search Authorization Summary Records Using Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user requests to view authorization details, the system must search the Authorization Summary data store using the Account ID to locate the parent summary record before retrieving any authorization detail records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a search of the Authorization Summary data store using the Account ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search returns a successful result indicating the Authorization Summary record exists for the given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the authorization record set status as 'Not End of Records' (AUTHS-NOT-EOF) and proceeds to retrieve the Authorization Detail record associated with the selected Authorization Key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Summary Record Successfully Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Authorization Summary record is successfully located using the Account ID, the system marks the record set as active (not at end) and proceeds to retrieve the corresponding Authorization Detail record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a search of the Authorization Summary data store using the Account ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search result indicates either that no Authorization Summary record exists for the given Account ID (record not found) OR the end of the Authorization Summary data store has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the authorization record set status as 'End of Records' (AUTHS-EOF) and stops all further authorization detail retrieval processing for this request, returning no authorization details to the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Summary Record Not Found or End of Database Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the search for an Authorization Summary record using the Account ID yields no matching record or the end of the data store is reached, the system marks the record set as exhausted and stops any further authorization detail retrieval processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An Authorization Summary record search has been performed for a given Account ID, and the result of that search is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to search for the Authorization Detail record using the Authorization Key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to search for the Authorization Detail record ONLY IF the Authorization Summary record was found (status is Not End of File); if the summary was not found (status is End of File), the detail record search is skipped entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prerequisite Check Before Searching Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must only attempt to retrieve an Authorization Detail record if the parent Authorization Summary record was successfully located. This ensures that detail record searches are always performed within the context of a valid summary.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Authorization Summary record has been located for the given Account ID, and an Authorization Key (selected pending authorization) is available in the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches for the Authorization Detail record within the Authorization Detail data store (PAUTDTL1) under the located summary
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Authorization Detail record whose Authorization Key matches the selected pending authorization key (PAUT9CTS = PA-AUTHORIZATION-KEY), and the full authorization detail data is loaded into the working area (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search Authorization Detail Record Using Authorization Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid Authorization Summary has been located, the system uses the Authorization Key to search for the specific Authorization Detail record within the scope of that summary. The Authorization Key is the unique identifier used to match the correct detail record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched for an Authorization Detail record in PAUTDTL1 using the Authorization Key under the located Authorization Summary
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Authorization Detail record is found successfully (search returns a normal/OK status)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the authorization retrieval status to 'Not End of File', indicating that a valid Authorization Detail record has been retrieved and is available for display and processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Record Found Successfully
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system successfully locates the Authorization Detail record matching the Authorization Key, it marks the retrieval status as active (Not End of File), allowing subsequent processing to use the retrieved detail data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched for an Authorization Detail record in PAUTDTL1 using the Authorization Key under the located Authorization Summary
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Authorization Detail record is not found (no matching record exists for the given Authorization Key) OR the end of the authorization detail data has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the authorization retrieval status to 'End of File', indicating that no Authorization Detail record is available for the given Authorization Key, and no detail data is populated for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Record Not Found or No More Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system cannot locate an Authorization Detail record matching the Authorization Key — either because no matching record exists or because the end of available records has been reached — it marks the retrieval status as End of File, signaling that no detail data is available for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched for an Authorization Detail record in PAUTDTL1 using the Authorization Key under the located Authorization Summary
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search returns an unexpected result that is neither a successful retrieval, a record-not-found condition, nor an end-of-database condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator to 'Y', composes an error message stating 'System error while reading Auth Details' along with the specific error status code returned, and immediately displays this error message to the user on the Authorization Detail View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Error During Authorization Detail Record Search
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected condition occurs while searching for the Authorization Detail record — any condition other than a successful retrieval, record not found, or end of database — the system treats this as a system error and immediately notifies the user with an error message on the Authorization Detail screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a specific pending authorization record on the Authorization Detail screen, and the session contains a valid Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) and a selected Authorization Key (CDEMO-CPVD-PAU-SELECTED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user initiates a fraud marking action (PF5) on the selected authorization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current authorization record from the Pending Authorization database using the Account ID and the Authorization Key as lookup criteria, making the latest authorization details available for fraud status evaluation and update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Authorization Record for Fraud Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any fraud status change can be made, the system must retrieve the current authorization record from the database using the Account ID and the selected Authorization Key to ensure the latest authorization data is used for fraud processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current authorization record has been retrieved from the database and its fraud status is already set to FRAUD CONFIRMED (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF5 to toggle the fraud status of this authorization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the authorization fraud status flag to FRAUD REMOVED (PA-FRAUD-REMOVED = TRUE) and sets the action indicator to WS-REMOVE-FRAUD = TRUE, marking this record for fraud removal processing before passing it to the fraud management program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remove Fraud Confirmation from Already-Flagged Authorization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization has already been confirmed as fraudulent, pressing PF5 toggles the fraud status by removing the fraud confirmation flag and marking the record for fraud removal processing, effectively reversing the prior fraud designation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current authorization record has been retrieved from the database and its fraud status is NOT set to FRAUD CONFIRMED (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF5 to toggle the fraud status of this authorization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the authorization fraud status flag to FRAUD CONFIRMED (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED = TRUE) and sets the action indicator to WS-REPORT-FRAUD = TRUE, marking this record for fraud reporting before passing it to the fraud management program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm New Fraud on Authorization Not Previously Flagged
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization has not previously been flagged as fraudulent, pressing PF5 confirms the authorization as fraud by setting the fraud confirmed flag and marking the record for fraud reporting, initiating the fraud reporting workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The fraud status flag on the authorization record has been updated (either set to FRAUD CONFIRMED or FRAUD REMOVED) based on the toggle decision
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Fraud Data Package to be sent to the external fraud management program (COPAUS2C)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the complete updated authorization detail record (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS) into the Fraud Data Package (WS-FRAUD-AUTH-RECORD), ensuring all authorization fields including the updated fraud status flag are included in the package

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Updated Authorization Details into Fraud Data Package
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the fraud status flag has been toggled (either confirmed or removed), the complete updated authorization detail record must be copied into the Fraud Data Package so that the external fraud management program receives the full and current authorization information including the updated fraud status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Fraud Data Package (WS-FRAUD-DATA) is being prepared with the updated authorization details and the session contains the Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) of the cardholder
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Fraud Data Package before calling the external fraud management program (COPAUS2C)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns the Account ID from the current session (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to the Account ID field within the Fraud Data Package (WS-FRD-ACCT-ID), ensuring the fraud action is linked to the correct account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Account ID to Fraud Data Package
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID associated with the authorization must be explicitly assigned to the Fraud Data Package so that the external fraud management program can correctly identify and associate the fraud action with the correct account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Fraud Data Package (WS-FRAUD-DATA) is being prepared with the updated authorization details and Account ID, and the session contains the Customer ID (CDEMO-CUST-ID) of the cardholder
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the Fraud Data Package before calling the external fraud management program (COPAUS2C)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns the Customer ID from the current session (CDEMO-CUST-ID) to the Customer ID field within the Fraud Data Package (WS-FRD-CUST-ID), ensuring the fraud action is linked to the correct customer, and the Fraud Data Package is now fully prepared and ready for submission to COPAUS2C

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Customer ID to Fraud Data Package
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer ID associated with the account must be explicitly assigned to the Fraud Data Package so that the external fraud management program can correctly identify and associate the fraud action with the correct customer record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Fraud Data Package (WS-FRAUD-DATA) has been fully populated with the updated authorization details (WS-FRAUD-AUTH-RECORD), the toggled fraud status flag (FRAUD CONFIRMED or FRAUD REMOVED), the Account ID (WS-FRD-ACCT-ID), and the Customer ID (WS-FRD-CUST-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to process the fraud status change
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system calls the external fraud management program COPAUS2C (WS-PGM-AUTH-FRAUD) via a program LINK, passing the complete Fraud Data Package (WS-FRAUD-DATA) as the communication area, delegating the fraud update persistence to the external program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke External Fraud Management Program with Prepared Fraud Data Package
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the Fraud Data Package is fully prepared with the updated authorization details, fraud status flag, Account ID, and Customer ID, the system must invoke the external fraud management program (COPAUS2C) to process and persist the fraud status change.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Account ID is available in the current session and an authorization record read has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve the Authorization Summary record from the Pending Authorization Summary data store using the Account ID as the unique search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Summary record matching the provided Account ID is retrieved and made available for the subsequent Authorization Detail retrieval step; the record retrieval status is captured for independent evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Authorization Summary Record Using Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When reading an authorization record, the system first retrieves the Authorization Summary record from the database using the Account ID as the search key. This is the mandatory first step before any authorization detail can be accessed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to retrieve the Authorization Summary record using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a successful status indicating the Authorization Summary record was found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the record set as 'not end of records' and proceeds to retrieve the Authorization Detail record using the Authorization Key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Summary Record Found - Proceed to Detail Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to retrieve the Authorization Summary record, the system independently evaluates the retrieval status. Only when the summary record is successfully found does the system proceed to retrieve the Authorization Detail record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to retrieve the Authorization Summary record using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a 'record not found' status or an 'end of database' status for the Authorization Summary retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the authorization record set as 'end of records', no Authorization Detail retrieval is attempted, and the read operation concludes with no record available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Summary Record Not Found - Mark End of Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Authorization Summary record cannot be found for the given Account ID, the system marks the end of records condition and stops further processing of the authorization record retrieval. No Authorization Detail retrieval is attempted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Summary record has been successfully retrieved for the given Account ID and the record set is marked as 'not end of records'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve the Authorization Detail record from the Pending Authorization Detail data store using the Authorization Key as the search criterion, within the context of the previously retrieved summary
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Detail record matching the provided Authorization Key is retrieved and made available for display and processing; the detail retrieval status is captured independently for evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Authorization Detail Record Using Authorization Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only after successfully retrieving the Authorization Summary record, the system retrieves the Authorization Detail record using the Authorization Key as the search criterion. This is a dependent second step that only executes when the summary record was found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Summary record was successfully retrieved and the system has attempted to retrieve the Authorization Detail record using the Authorization Key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a successful status indicating the Authorization Detail record was found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the authorization record set as 'not end of records' and the complete authorization record (both summary and detail) is considered successfully retrieved and available for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Record Found - Mark Successful Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to retrieve the Authorization Detail record, the system independently evaluates the detail retrieval status. When the detail record is successfully found, the overall authorization record retrieval is marked as successfully completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Authorization Summary record was successfully retrieved and the system has attempted to retrieve the Authorization Detail record using the Authorization Key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a 'record not found' status or an 'end of database' status for the Authorization Detail retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the authorization record set as 'end of records' and the read operation concludes with no complete authorization record available for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Record Not Found - Mark End of Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Authorization Detail record cannot be found for the given Authorization Key (even though the summary was found), the system marks the end of records condition. This is an independent status check separate from the summary record check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization record read has been initiated with a valid Account ID and Authorization Key available in the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the two-step retrieval: Step 1 - retrieve Authorization Summary by Account ID; Step 2 (conditional on Step 1 success) - retrieve Authorization Detail by Authorization Key; each step independently evaluates its retrieval outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If both steps succeed, the full authorization record is marked as successfully retrieved and available; if either step fails to find a record (not found or end of data), the record set is marked as 'end of records' and no further retrieval is attempted for that step or any subsequent step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Two-Step Sequential Authorization Record Retrieval with Independent Status Checks
all_rules.Rule_Description: The complete authorization record retrieval is a mandatory two-step sequential process: first the Authorization Summary must be found using Account ID, and only then is the Authorization Detail retrieved using the Authorization Key. Each step has its own independent success/failure evaluation, and the second step is only attempted when the first step succeeds.

description:
COPAUS1C is an online CICS COBOL program within the CardDemo Authorization Module that provides a detailed view of a pending authorization message for a given account. It allows users to view authorization details such as card number, transaction amount, merchant information, and response codes, and also enables marking or removing a fraud flag on a specific authorization record. The program interacts with an IMS database to read and update pending authorization segments, and delegates fraud processing to a linked program (COPAUS2C).
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: IMS - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize error flags, erase flags, and clear message fields at program startup 2: New Session Redirect - When no communication area exists, redirect user back to the Authorization Summary screen 3: First Entry Processing - On first entry to the screen, load and display the authorization detail record for the selected authorization 4: Screen Navigation Handling - Evaluate user keystrokes (Enter, PF3, PF5, PF8) and route to appropriate processing routines 5: Return to Authorization Summary - On PF3 key press, navigate back to the Authorization Summary screen 6: Mark/Unmark Authorization as Fraud - On PF5 key press, toggle the fraud status of the current authorization record (mark as fraud or remove fraud flag) 7: Navigate to Next Authorization - On PF8 key press, advance to the next authorization detail record for the account 8: Invalid Key Handling - Display an invalid key message when an unsupported function key is pressed 9: Authorization Record Retrieval - Read the authorization summary and detail records from the database using the account ID and authorization key 10: Next Authorization Record Retrieval - Read the next sequential authorization detail record from the database for forward navigation 11: End of Authorization Records Detection - Detect when there are no more authorization records and display 'Already at the last Authorization' message 12: Authorization Detail Display Population - Populate screen fields with authorization details including card number, date, time, amount, response code, decline reason, processing code, POS entry mode, message source, merchant category code, card expiry date, authorization type, transaction ID, match status, fraud status, and merchant information 13: Authorization Response Code Interpretation - Determine if authorization was Approved (code '00') or Declined and display appropriate indicator with color coding (green for approved, red for declined) 14: Decline Reason Code Lookup - Search the decline reason table to find and display the description corresponding to the authorization response reason code 15: Fraud Status Display - Display fraud flag and fraud report date if the authorization has been confirmed as fraud or had fraud removed; otherwise display a dash 16: Fraud Confirmation Toggle - When marking fraud, check current fraud status: if already confirmed as fraud then remove it, if not fraudulent then mark it as fraud 17: Fraud Processing Delegation - Pass authorization details, account ID, and customer ID to the fraud processing program (COPAUS2C) for fraud status update 18: Fraud Update Success Handling - If fraud program returns success, update the authorization detail record in the database and display success message ('AUTH MARKED FRAUD' or 'AUTH FRAUD REMOVED') 19: Fraud Update Failure Handling - If fraud program returns failure, rollback database changes and display the error message returned from the fraud program 20: Authorization Detail Record Update - Save updated authorization details (with new fraud status and report date) back to the database 21: Transaction Commit - Commit database changes after a successful authorization detail update 22: Transaction Rollback - Rollback database changes when an error occurs during fraud tagging or update operations 23: Screen Header Population - Populate screen header with application title, transaction ID, program name, current date, and current time 24: Authorization Detail Screen Display - Send the populated authorization detail screen to the user terminal, with full erase or partial refresh depending on navigation context 25: Screen Input Receipt - Receive user input from the authorization detail screen 26: Date and Time Formatting - Format authorization original date from YYMMDD to MM/DD/YY display format and format time with colon separators for display 27: Card Expiry Date Formatting - Format card expiry date by inserting a slash separator between month and year for display
